cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1,375 very preterm infants with a birth weight less than 1,500g, born between 2016 and 2021.
finding: Cesarean section reduced early mortality in very preterm infants under 28 weeks' gestation but increased respiratory morbidity at 28-31(+6) weeks, with no significant impact on other analyzed outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with reduced early mortality in very preterm infants less than 28 weeks' gestation but increased respiratory morbidity in those 28-31(+6) weeks' gestation compared to vaginal delivery.
followup_time: Outcomes were assessed during the neonatal period, with early mortality specifically measured within 3 days after birth.
gest_age: Very preterm infants, specifically analyzed in categories of <28 weeks and 28-31(+6) weeks.
